page: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.large is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at up to 3.9 GHz. It features an x86_64 architecture with 2 virtual CPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads. The instance incorporates burstable CPU allocation and provides a large 480 MB L3 cache, along with support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM clocked at 7 GHz, providing a generous 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage and relies entirely on external network-attached block storage. Additionally, it features no GPU hardware acceleration and reports a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded capabilities alongside expected multi-core scaling limitations. In single-core tests, the instance demonstrated strong performance in Geekbench (2159.0), single-threaded gzip compression (33.89 GB/sec), and text processing. However, multi-core throughput in Geekbench (2719.0) and stress-ng multi-core testing placed lower relative to larger multi-core hardware, reflecting the constraint of a single underlying physical core. Uncached memory read bandwidth also showed lower throughput in large-block tests.

The r8i-flex.large offers an entry-level, cost-conscious path to high memory capacity per core. Because it leverages a burstable CPU tier without bundled local storage, it provides budget efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand sustained 100% CPU utilization. Appropriate workloads include lightweight Redis or Memcached instances, test and development databases, bursty microservices, and memory-sensitive data preprocessing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro System. Driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, it supplies 2 burstable vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core and 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory. The instance features no local storage and zero GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage. Benchmark data reflects strong single-core performance in compute and compression tests, though multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth are limited by the single-core topology. The generous 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a cost-efficient profile for memory-heavy applications with intermittent compute demands. It is suited for lightweight caching layers, small databases, and memory-dependent background tasks.
